description: A wide 16:9 sequence diagram of one tool call, read top to bottom, with three tall vertical lanes drawn as rounded columns. Left lane header: 'Our code (Ask Northbridge)'. Middle lane header: 'LLM (gemini-3.8-flash)'. Right lane header: 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2'. Six numbered horizontal arrows going down the page in this order: arrow 1 from 'Our code' to 'LLM' labelled '1  messages + tool definitions'. Arrow 2 from 'LLM' back to 'Our code' labelled '2  tool call: check_stock, item_code BAT-500'. Arrow 3 from 'Our code' to 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2' labelled '3  checked, then run in Emma's session'. Arrow 4 from 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2' back to 'Our code' labelled '4  5,400 on hand in Manchester'. Arrow 5 from 'Our code' to 'LLM' labelled '5  tool result'. Arrow 6 from 'LLM' to 'Our code' labelled '6  the answer in words'. A thin dashed vertical barrier between the LLM lane and the Ledgerline lane with the small label 'the model never touches Ledgerline'. Arrows 1, 2, 5 and 6 in sky blue, arrows 3 and 4 in ember orange. The three lane headers are exactly 'Our code (Ask Northbridge)', 'LLM (gemini-3.8-flash)' and 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2', and nothing above them. Do not add any column headers, row headers, section titles or labels other than the ones quoted here. Labels as plain text, no brackets.

A wide 16:9 left-to-right flow diagram of what happens inside one tool. Far left, a sky-blue rounded box 'The model's request' with a small code line under it 'check_stock, item_code BAT-500'. An arrow to a green-outlined box 'tool.json' with the subtitle 'checks the request at the door'. An arrow to a dark-grey box 'tool.py' with the subtitle 'run(s, item_code)'. From tool.py three thin ember-orange arrows fan out to three small ember-orange boxes stacked vertically: 'itm_get  ITEM MASTER GET', 'whs_list  WAREHOUSE LIST', 'stk_query  STOCK STATUS ENQUIRY'. Each of the three returns a small grey tag 'rc, err_cd, msg, data'. The three replies join into one arrow back to tool.py, then an arrow to a sky-blue box at the far right 'One clean result' with the subtitle 'ok, warehouses, free_total, cover_days'. Draw a large light-grey shaded rounded region behind tool.json, tool.py and the three services, with the small label at its bottom 'inside the tool: never in the model's context'. Do not add any column headers, row headers, section titles or labels other than the ones quoted here. Labels as plain text, no brackets.

A wide 16:9 figure with two panels side by side, separated by a thin vertical rule. LEFT panel caption at its top: 'Without a standard: N x M'. In it, a column of 4 rounded boxes on the left labelled 'Ask Northbridge', 'Claude Code', 'Claude Desktop', 'Workflow Studio', and a column of 3 rounded boxes on the right labelled 'Ledgerline toolbox', 'Policy library', 'E-mail'. Every left box is joined to every right box by its own thin ember-orange line, 12 lines in total, crossing like a tangle; a small note under the panel: '4 apps x 3 systems = 12 integrations'. RIGHT panel caption at its top: 'With MCP: N + M'. The same 4 app boxes on the left and the same 3 system boxes on the right, but each app has one short sky-blue line into a single tall central vertical bar labelled 'MCP', and each system box has one short sky-blue line from that bar, 7 lines in total; a small note under the panel: '4 + 3 = 7 connections'. Labels as plain text, no brackets.

A wide 16:9 architecture diagram of the three MCP roles, left to right. On the LEFT a large rounded container labelled 'Host' with the subtitle 'the app the person uses: Claude Code or Ask Northbridge'. Inside the host, top: a box 'LLM'. Inside the host, bottom: a box 'MCP client'. In the MIDDLE, one horizontal double-headed arrow from the client box, labelled 'JSON-RPC: initialize, tools/list, tools/call'. On the RIGHT a green-outlined rounded box 'MCP server: ledgerline-toolbox' with the subtitle '16 tools'. To the far right of the server, an ember-orange box 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2' joined by a short line labelled 'Emma's session'. Under the figure three short captions aligned under each role: under Host 'holds the model and the conversation', under the arrow 'one client per server', under the server 'lists its tools and runs them'. Sky blue for host and client, green outline for the server, ember only for Ledgerline. Labels as plain text, no brackets.

A wide 16:9 figure with two panels side by side. LEFT panel title: 'stdio'. A box 'Claude Code' on the left and a box 'python -m ledgerline.toolbox.mcp --user ECLARKE' on the right, labelled underneath 'a child process on the same computer'. Between them two horizontal arrows, the top one labelled 'stdin: one JSON message per line', the bottom one going back labelled 'stdout: one JSON message per line'. RIGHT panel title: 'Streamable HTTP'. A box 'Ask Northbridge (web app)' on the left and a box 'ledgerline-toolbox at /mcp' on the right, labelled underneath 'a server on the network'. Between them two arrows, the top one labelled 'POST /mcp: the JSON-RPC message', the bottom one going back labelled 'reply: JSON or a stream of events'. Under both panels a single centred line: 'the same JSON-RPC messages, two different pipes'. Labels as plain text, no brackets.

A wide 16:9 diagram of two harnesses sharing one tool server. TOP LEFT a large rounded container labelled 'Claude's harness: Claude Code' with three small grey boxes inside: 'Anthropic's system prompt', 'Claude decides the steps', 'approve each call in the app'. TOP RIGHT a large sky-blue rounded container labelled 'Our harness: Ask Northbridge' with five small sky-blue boxes inside: 'our system prompt and model', 'which tools each person sees', 'guard before every write', 'loop limit: 14 rounds', 'every call logged, tokens and cost'. From the bottom of each container one arrow goes down into the SAME single green-outlined box in the bottom centre labelled 'MCP server: ledgerline-toolbox'. Below that box a short line to an ember-orange box 'Ledgerline ERP 7.2'. Do not add any column headers, row headers, section titles or labels other than the ones quoted here. Labels as plain text, no brackets.
